title: Wounds that bench survivors
overseerSummary: Two builders proposed this independently. Merged: trigger on the lowest HP a survivor reached in any fight (end HP is erased by regen), recovery scaled by lodging and food, and a greyed 'recovering, back in N' row in the picker. One writer, inside the debrief.

proposals.title: Sorties leave wounds from the lowest HP a survivor reached, so the roster has to rotate
proposals.problem: A returning squad is as fresh as one that never left. c.injured is never set in the browser, stamina is not spent by a Field sortie, and out-of-fight regen restores HP before the squad is home. The same four characters can run contracts back to back, limited only by clicks, and the rest of the roster never leaves town. The injury system exists in full (20 consumer sites) and has no producer.
evidence: missions.js:265-266 the only assignment of c.injured, in the branch taken when Roster is undefined; game.html loads roster.js, so the browser never takes it

consumers that never see a nonzero value: condition.js:146 (morale target -15), temper.js:259-260, crew.js:249 and 475, game.js:651 and 664 (rota), quests.js:136 and 155, sortie.js:206, 899, 1018 (party pickers), townlife.js:53 and 62

missions.js:167 decrements c.injured for every character on every town tick; game.js:402-408 is the per-character loop that already holds restFor(c) and fedTown for Condition.tick; condition.js:49 exports FED_REST
sortie.js settle() (439-541) does not call Condition.spend; missions.js:259 does for Gate runs (25 + 1.5 x level + casts)
sortie.js:23 and 370-378 REGEN 0.005 of max HP per in-game second out of a fight, so end-of-run HP is not a wound signal; a sample taken after each fight in resolve() (sortie.js:155) is
field.js:1939-1943 ACTOR_KEYS is the saved-actor key list; 'noFightUntil' is listed twice (1942 and 1943), harmless but removed in the same edit

MEASURED, combat.js runner (900 sorties, 3-5 stars, 70% won), lowest end-of-fight HP fraction per survivor: p10 0.29, p25 0.64, p50 0.89; below 0.9 for 52%, below 0.5 for 18%, below 0.3 for 10%, below 0.15 for 4%. The attrition-resolver figures in the original proposal understated the dips.

MEASURED, rule injured = round(30 x clamp((WOUND_FROM - low) / WOUND_FROM, 0, 1)): WOUND_FROM 0.6 injures 22.3% of survivors and 49% of sorties; 0.5: 18.0% / 43%; 0.45: 16.4% / 40%; 0.4: 14.3% of survivors, 37% of sorties (18% of won sorties), mean 13.9 ticks among the injured, mean longest wait 16.1 ticks (about 2.7 min) in sorties that have one; 0.3: 10.2% / 30%

MEASURED, REGEN sensitivity (the 'missed' list asked for it): REGEN 0.0025 / 0.001 / 0.0002 gives wins 68% / 67% / 67% and deaths 0.29 / 0.33 / 0.34 per sortie against 70% / 0.298 at 0.005; the low-point distribution barely moves. REGEN is not the constant that decides attrition and does not need retuning for wounds to work.

MEASURED, healing: survivors in squads with a support role are injured at W=0.4 in 12.6% of cases against 16.2% without (mean 1.66 vs 2.19 injured ticks per survivor); squads with a Cleric 12.3% vs 16.3%. Sampling at fight end already counts in-fight healing.
median sortie clock 286 in-game s = 57 real s at 1x (condition.js header: a town tick is 10 s; INJURY_TICKS 30 = 5 min, missions.js:25, 290)
proposals.change:
1. field.js: add 'low' to ACTOR_KEYS (field.js:1939-1943) so a resumed run keeps it, and delete the duplicate 'noFightUntil'.
2. sortie.js resolve(), after C.encounter (sortie.js:176): for (const a of ours) if (a.fighter && a.fighter.alive) a.low = Math.min(a.low === undefined ? 1 : a.low, a.fighter.hp / a.fighter.maxHp). End-of-fight HP, so healing and potions used inside the fight count.
3. sortie.js settle(), per survivor c with actor a: c.injured = max(c.injured, round(Missions.INJURY_TICKS x clamp((WOUND_FROM - a.low) / WOUND_FROM, 0, 1))) with WOUND_FROM = 0.4, and c.woundNote = { low: a.low, where: m.name } for display. INJURY_TICKS is already exported (missions.js:290). Stamina and caster-pool spend is NOT added here: it belongs to the shared per-survivor debrief hook (Missions.debrief, systems-one-debrief). If that proposal is not approved, add the single call Condition.spend(c, { staminaCost: 25 + m.level * 1.5, casts }) at this same site, so it exists in one place only.
4. Recovery rate: move the decrement out of missions.js:167 into Missions.recover(c, rate = 1), called from the game.js per-character loop (game.js:402-408) with rate = restFor(c) x (fedTown ? Condition.FED_REST : 1). Lodging.restFor is 0.90-1.60, so a 30-tick wound heals in about 15-33 ticks depending on bed and meals. Offline catch-up runs the same tick() so it stays consistent. c.injured becomes fractional; displays use Math.ceil; clear c.woundNote when it reaches 0.
5. Log one line per run, not per person: 'Bram is out for 14 ticks: dropped to 18% HP at Goblin Camp'.
6. Party picker (sortie.js:899, 1018): list injured characters greyed with 'back in N min, dropped to X% at <mission>' instead of omitting them. Board header: 'N recovering, first back in X min' (sum c.injured x TICK_MS per character, minimum over the roster).
7. Calibration check before ship: log a.low for one browser session on a real save and confirm the share of survivors injured is 12-16% and of sorties 30-40%; adjust WOUND_FROM only.
proposals.playerEffect: After a sortie the question becomes who goes next: wait up to 5 minutes for the wounded group, send the bench now, or carry potions and a support role so the low point stays above the threshold (measured: 3.6 points fewer injured survivors with a support role). Bench characters acquire a use. The cost is visible: the picker shows who is back when and why they are out.
proposals.secondOrder: Healing potions and support classes lift the low point, so Outfit's potion supply and the alchemist trade reduce downtime and not only deaths. Bed quality and meals set who is back first (restFor, FED_REST), so the Field depends on the Town tab's lodging. Injured members sit at home with a -15 morale target (condition.js:146), which feeds Condition.moraleMult and town output. Trials do not list injured owners (quests.js:136), so timing a trial becomes a planning question. The rota and the Hone/Staffing screens already skip injured characters (game.js:651, 664; crew.js:249, 475). Stamina and pool spend arrive through the shared debrief, so a squad that sorties twice in a row also opens its second fight with smaller pools (combat.js:83-88).
proposals.risks: More waiting for an active player: 37% of sorties leave at least one member out, mean longest wait 2.7 minutes, worst case 5, while a median sortie is under a minute of watching; a roster of 4-5 feels it fully, a roster of 8+ rotates. Quests.offers drops injured owners from the trial list (quests.js:136), so trial cards disappear and reappear; list them greyed if that proves confusing. Moving the decrement changes missions.js tick for node-only callers (no recovery without game.js); the Gate's Roster-undefined branch is legacy. The thresholds come from plain characters without gear or potions (the runner's limit), so confirm in the browser as in step 7. Interaction with loop-retreat: a retreating squad takes more hits on the walk out, so wounds are part of the price of retreating.
proposals.response: Design attack ('cooldown dressed as a decision', the low-point rule ignores healing after the dip): sampling is at the end of each fight, after in-fight healing and potions, and the data shows it responds to healers (12.6% vs 16.2% injured with a support role). Out-of-fight regen cannot heal anyone because REGEN only acts on HP and the sample is already taken. A large roster not feeling it is intended: it is the bench acquiring a use. The stamina term (about 1.5 minutes of rest) is dropped from this proposal and left to the shared debrief. Design demand (one implementation with systems-wounds-via-injured, a.low trigger, restFor x fed recovery, one hook, greyed picker row, calibrate from combat.js and state the share of sorties): all accepted. The calibration was done on combat.js and moved WOUND_FROM from 0.6 to 0.4: at 0.6 the rule would have injured 22% of survivors and 49% of sorties, not the 14% the attrition model gave. Engineering demands 1-4: same set; combined downtime budget is stated as 12-16% of survivors, 30-40% of sorties, mean wait 2.3 min; the stamina/pool ETA is for the debrief owner to show next to this one in the picker.

verdicts.attack: It is a cooldown dressed as a decision: with Skip a sortie takes seconds, so 'who goes next' is a 2-5 minute wait or a bench pick, and a roster with eight idle 3-stars never feels it. The low-point rule ignores healing after the dip, so a Cleric who brought someone back from 15% still sends them to bed, which contradicts the claim that healers reduce downtime. The stamina term (25 + 1.5 x level) is about 1.5 minutes of rest at condition.js:168, i.e. nothing.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: c.injured has no browser writer (missions.js:265-266 is the Roster-undefined branch; game.js:93 only defaults it to 0) and readers at sortie.js:206, 1018; crew.js:249, 475; condition.js:146, 151; quests.js:136, 155; game.js:651, 664, 1180; townlife.js:53, 62. missions.js:167 decrements it every town tick via game.js:470. REGEN 0.005/s at sortie.js:23, 370-378 makes end-of-run HP meaningless (full in 200 in-game s). combat.js:83-88 reads staminaFrac/poolFrac at fighter build. The 14% injured rate and the low-point distribution come from the attrition resolver and are unverified in combat.js.
verdicts.demand: One implementation shared with systems-wounds-via-injured: trigger on a.low (REGEN erases end HP), recover with the restFor x fed scaled decrement from the systems version, and write it inside the single debrief hook from systems-one-debrief so Condition.spend is not called twice. The picker shows recovering characters greyed with the tick count and the low point that caused it, instead of omitting them. Calibrate WOUND_FROM from a.low logged in real combat.js fights over one session, and state the resulting share of sorties that leave at least one member unavailable.

verdicts.attack: WOUND_FROM and the 15% injury rate come from the attrition resolver with invented squad power/hp (test/field.harness.js:38), not from combat.js low points; it adds up to 5 minutes of downtime per sortie on top of systems-one-debrief's stamina and caster-pool costs with no combined budget; Quests.offers (quests.js:136) drops injured characters so trial cards appear and disappear; it is the same feature as systems-wounds-via-injured.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified missions.js:265-266 is the only assignment of c.injured and sits in the Roster-undefined branch; game.js:93 initialises it to 0; roster.js loads at game.html:520; 20 reader sites by grep; missions.js:167 decrements inside Missions.tick, called from game.js:470 every tick including catchUp (MAX_OFFLINE_TICKS 2880); settle() (sortie.js:439-541) never calls Condition.spend, only Condition.outcome at 517; REGEN 0.005/s at sortie.js:23, 370-378 so end-of-run HP is not a wound signal, which is why the low-point rule is the right one; Missions.INJURY_TICKS = 30 exported (missions.js:25, 290); Condition.spend exists (condition.js:184-190); game.js:104-106 skips Condition.tick for c.mission.
verdicts.demand: 1) This is the single wound implementation: fold in systems-wounds' recovery tick scaled by Lodging.restFor(state, c) x (fed ? FED_REST : 1) and its folded 'recovering, back in N' picker row. 2) Add 'low' to ACTOR_KEYS and log a.low for one browser session before fixing WOUND_FROM. 3) The per-survivor hook lives in the shared debrief from systems-one-debrief, not a second loop over run.party. 4) State a combined downtime target with systems-one-debrief (ticks until a 4-person squad is fully available after a clean win).

proposals.title: Carry wounds home through the existing injured counter, healed by bed and food
proposals.problem: Every sortie starts at full HP and a survivor at 5% HP loses nothing afterwards, so the only cost of risk is death. c.injured, the counter that blocks launching (sortie.js:206), crew staffing, morale, where the character walks and the sheet text 'recovering (N ticks)', is set only by a Node-only fallback (missions.js:265-266), so that code is unreachable in the browser. The earlier draft measured end HP on single combat.js fights and was challenged because sortie.js regenerates 0.5% of max HP per in-game second out of a fight (sortie.js:23, 370-378). Re-measured through a copy of the full sortie loop including that regen (1,800 runs, 15 types): when settle() runs, 28% of survivors are under 85% HP, 16% under 60% and 7% under 30% (p25 0.79, median 1.00). The regen does not hide the damage between fights either: 45% of fights after the first start with the party's mean HP under 90% and 28% under 70% (240 runs, 6.7 fights per run).
evidence: combat.js:72 `hp: d.hp, maxHp: d.hp` on every fighter build; sortie.js:370-378 REGEN 0.005 of max HP and pool per in-game second out of a fight (not under the 'dry' twist). 200 in-game seconds to full = 40 real seconds.

missions.js:265-266 `if (typeof Roster !== 'undefined') { Roster.fall(...) } else c.injured = INJURY_TICKS`; Roster is always loaded in the browser. missions.js:167 decrements injured by 1 per tick for everyone.

Readers of c.injured: sortie.js:206, 1018 (the picker omits injured characters); crew.js staffing; condition.js:146 (morale -15); temper.js hardship; townlife.js:53; townview.js:131; game.js:651, 664, 993, 1180, 1387, 2307-2308.

Scratch real.js / wounds.js (copy of the sortie loop), 300 runs, 279 with a survivor: wound = loss >= 0.15 of max HP at settle gives >= 1 injured member in 50% of sorties, 27% of survivors injured; at WOUND_TICKS 120 the mean among injured is 62 ticks (p90 101), at 80 it is 41 (p90 67). Nadir variant (lowest HP during the run, loop lens): nadir loss >= 0.4 injures >= 1 member in 68% of sorties, mean 84 ticks at 120.

Scratch rostersim.js over those measured loss vectors: a squad of 4 launched every 8 ticks, always the first four ready, WOUND_TICKS 80: roster 8 blocks 21% of launches at rest x1.0 and 6% at x1.8 (manor, fed), 43% and 29% of the roster unavailable; roster 15 blocks 0%, unavailable 30% and 17%; roster 30 blocks 0%, unavailable 15% and 8%. WOUND_TICKS 120 at roster 8 blocks 38% and 16%. Launching every 15 ticks at roster 8, WOUND_TICKS 80: blocks 5% and 0%.
condition.js tick() already receives restMult (game.js:408 `restMult: restFor(c)`, lodging.js:178-181: tent 0.90 to sanctum 1.60, 0.75 roofless) and `fed`; FED_REST = 1.25 (condition.js:49).
proposals.change: 1) condition.js: wound(c, lost) sets c.injured = max(c.injured, ceil(WOUND_TICKS x lost)) when lost >= WOUND_FROM; WOUND_FROM 0.15, WOUND_TICKS 80. Missions.debrief (systems-one-debrief) calls it once per survivor with lost = 1 - end HP fraction (Field: fighter.hp / maxHp at settle; Gate: run.members[id].hp). The trigger is the argument of this one function, so the nadir variant replaces only that argument. 2) condition.js tick(): when c.injured > 0, injured -= restMult x (fed ? FED_REST : 1) x (job ? 0.5 : 1), floored at 0. The flat decrement at missions.js:167 is removed. No Lodging accessor is needed in missions.js, which also loads in field.html and Node. 3) Condition.recovery(c, restMult, fed) returns { wound, rate, ticks }; game.js exposes it on window.Game. The sheet text at game.js:993, 1180 and 1387 prints 'recovering: 48 wound ticks, about 27 ticks at rest x1.45, fed'. 4) sortie.js picker: characters with injured > 0 are listed in a folded 'Recovering' row under the party grid with that ETA, instead of being omitted at sortie.js:1018.
proposals.playerEffect: Sending the 30%-HP veteran again, or waiting about 25 to 40 ticks, is a decision the game never offers now, and it is a death-prevention decision: a wounded character in the next squad is one the player chose to send. Roster depth gains value (a second squad covers the first one's recovery). Lodging tier, bed rules and the kitchen turn into recovery speed: manor rest x1.45 with a fed pantry heals 1.8 wound ticks per tick, a tent unfed 0.9.
proposals.secondOrder: The -15 morale for injury (condition.js:146) and the temper hardship terms start working, so a wounded character is also a lower-morale one, which systems-will-axis reads. Townlife already walks injured characters to bed; Crew.hone and staffing already skip them. Meals gain a second effect through FED_REST on recovery as well as on rest. systems-one-debrief's 'ready in' figure includes the wound ETA. Offline catch-up heals everyone, so wounds matter during active play only.
proposals.risks: Recovery slows an idle game whose player may be away: at roster 8 the player is blocked on 6-21% of rapid launches; WOUND_TICKS is the single dial and the headless harness should report blocked launches at rosters of 8, 15 and 30 before it is accepted. At roster 15 and above the system is visible as unavailability (17-30%) but never blocks. Gate end HP includes a quarter-HP rest (missions.js:196), so Gate wounds are rarer than contract wounds. The end-HP trigger and the nadir trigger overlap with loop-wounds; this proposal commits to end HP because a settle-log line can print each survivor's HP, which makes the cause traceable, and 50% of sorties wound someone at that setting. If loop-wounds lands, keep steps 2 to 4 of this one and take its trigger.
proposals.response: Design attack: the trigger does fire under the real REGEN. At settle 28% of survivors are under 85% HP and 16% under 60% (1,800 combat-backed runs), and 28% of fights after the first begin below 70% party HP, so the 'REGEN restores everyone' premise does not hold for contracts; the 588-survivor sample in the earlier draft was single fights and is superseded by this measurement. I kept the end-HP trigger for traceability and show the nadir alternative's firing rate for the merge. Kept as requested: the restFor x fed healing tick (moved into Condition.tick, so no Lodging accessor in missions.js, which answers the engineering attack) and the folded 'Recovering' picker row with ETA. One writer: Missions.debrief. Roster sizes 8, 15 and 30 are tested above. WOUND_TICKS was lowered from 120 to 80 because 120 blocks 38% of launches at roster 8. Engineering attack that the trigger depends on map length: the measurement is over complete sorties including the walk home, and the settle log prints the HP that produced the wound.

verdicts.attack: The trigger does not fire in the real game: settle() runs after the walk home and REGEN (sortie.js:23, 370-378) restores 0.5% of max HP per in-game second out of a fight, so a survivor is full 200 in-game seconds (40 real seconds at 1x) after the last fight and 'lost = 1 - hp/maxHp >= 0.15' is almost never true. The 588-survivor sample is single combat.js encounters with no walk and no REGEN, which is not what settle() sees. WOUND_TICKS 120 (8 minutes for a 40% loss) is a guess against an idle player.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: combat.js:72 builds hp from derived each time; missions.js:165-167 and the readers as listed; lodging.js:178-181 restFor (0.90 tent to 1.60 sanctum, 0.75 roofless); condition.js:49 FED_REST 1.25; endhp.js in the scratchpad runs Combat.encounter with frontage 8 and no field regen, so its p50 0.85 end HP is a per-fight figure, not a per-sortie one.
verdicts.demand: Fold into loop-wounds: keep this proposal's restFor x fed scaled healing tick and the greyed 'recovering, ETA' picker row; drop the end-HP trigger for a.low; one writer inside Missions.debrief; test against roster sizes 8, 15 and 30 as proposed.

verdicts.attack: Its trigger is end-of-run HP loss >= 0.15, but sortie.js:370-378 regenerates 0.5% of max HP per in-game second for every actor out of a fight; a survivor who left the last fight at 40% and walked 60 tiles home (about 110 s at BASE_SPEED 0.55) plus PORTAL.open 20 s is back above the threshold, so whether a wound lands depends on map length, which the player cannot trace. Its evidence script measures single Combat.encounter matchups with no field regen. loop-wounds' low-point rule has the same consumers without this flaw.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified combat.js:72 full HP per fighter build (but fighters persist across skirmishes within one sortie, sortie.js:120-152, so only sorties start fresh); missions.js:265-266; the 20 reader sites; lodging.js:178 restFor and condition.js:49 FED_REST exist; REGEN at sortie.js:23; the builder's endhp.js header confirms it runs Combat.encounter per matchup, not Field runs.
verdicts.demand: Fold two pieces into loop-wounds: the recovery tick scaled by Lodging.restFor(state, c) x (fed ? FED_REST : 1), which needs an optional Lodging accessor in missions.js because field.html and Node do not load it, and the folded 'recovering, back in N' row in the party picker.
